Filed eight papers by hand into `inbox/` and read all eight. They are the
stopping-criterion cluster that the archive's RCP reading cites but never
held: Answer Convergence as a Signal for Early Stopping (2506.02536),
THOUGHTTERMINATOR (2504.13367), Correct Reasoning Paths Visit Shared Decision
Pivots (2509.21549), Revisiting Overthinking from the Perspective of
Self-Doubt (2505.23480), Certainty-Guided Reflection Suppression (2508.05337),
a token-complexity study of CoT compression (2503.01141), Early Stopping via
Confidence Dynamics (2604.04930) and Semantic-Preserving Early Exit
(2605.17672). None had ever been scored: all predate the collector's window,
so they were absent from `rejected.jsonl` and `seen.sqlite` alike. Two further
titles from the same reference list turned out to be already held under
different names — "Stop When Enough" is the paper this archive had recorded as
REFRAIN, and "Your Models Have Thought Enough" was already in.

**Answer Convergence (EMNLP 2025) is the RCP paper's direct precursor and
shares its instrument almost exactly** — NLTK sentence chunking, incremental
prefixes, a forced `</think>`, a greedy answer read out at each cut. Its
Answer Convergence Ratio is the Reasoning Completion Point normalised by trace
length, defined by string equality of the forced answer rather than by a KL
residual. It also records, a year earlier, the observation RCPD is built on:
`</think>` already sits in the top 10 candidates at sentence boundaries while
the model prefers "wait", "or", "but". RCPD's thresholds sit at 5 and 10. The
RCP paper cites this work but does not draw the connection.

That paper also supplies the negative result the cluster needed. On
R1-Qwen-32B its unsupervised Answer Consistency stopping improves NQ (35.0 ->
38.4) and GSM8K (89.4 -> 91.0) but destroys the hard end: MATH-500 91.0 ->
55.0, GPQA 33.3 -> 14.1, AIME'24 73.3 -> 13.3. Only the supervised activation
probe holds. That is the same difficulty boundary at which the archive's
multilingual latent-reasoning reading finds early answer formation vanishing
(LRS 0.38 on MGSM, 0.03 on Multilingual AIME), and the same ordering BLADE
reports. Worth noting against the paper itself: its main runs use alpha = 0.6
and k = 10 while its own ablations recommend alpha <= 0.4 and k in [20, 30],
and it evaluates MATH-500 on a 100-item subset.

**An independent reproduction of RCPD now exists in the archive, and it does
not reproduce.** Early Stopping via Confidence Dynamics (COLM 2026 workshop)
benchmarks six inference-time stopping methods on shared pre-generated
trajectories. RCPD's overall compression rate comes out at 96.9%, 91.3%,
100.0% and 96.2% across four models — between zero and nine percent of tokens
saved, against the up-to-44% its own paper reports. On Qwen3-14B, the one
model the two papers share, RCPD's own 60% CR becomes 91.3% here. Answer
Convergence fails in the opposite direction, compressing to 20.3% CR at 51.1
accuracy against vanilla's 78.4. This is not a settled refutation: the model
sets and benchmark mixes differ, and the reproduction reports Cost > Tok for
RCPD in every row, which suggests it generates intermediate answers where
published RCPD only reads a rank out of the existing next-token distribution.
Recorded as a finding about that protocol, with the mismatch named. It does
land on the gap the RCP reading already flagged — that RCPD is never validated
against its own gold stopping point.

That paper also contributes a metric the cluster has been missing: **Cost**,
total tokens including intermediate-answer overhead. Under it, Think or Not
costs more than vanilla (11668 against 8344 on Qwen3-4B) while generating
fewer reasoning tokens. The archive has flagged this accounting gap twice
before — ParaTempo excludes probe forward passes from its token counts, and
NEAT measured CGRS increasing wall-clock 41-63% while shortening output.
